title: hosted-api-enterprise-request-governance-and-sla-driven-prioritization
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create and pilot a governance-first intake and prioritization rubric for Hosted API enterprise feature requests focused on chat streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. Aim: give CS, Sales, and PMs a deterministic way to triage incoming non-bug requests (feature asks, SLA/throughput requirements, compliance needs) so we can route work to Hosted, Dedicated, or Private and set correct SLAs and rollout plans.
background: Over the last 6 months we've seen ambiguous enterprise asks arrive via support and sales (e.g., lower-latency streaming for tool-calls, structured-output schema validation, locked-down function-calling for regulated customers). Current intake is ad-hoc: PM judgement + CS context. That leads to inconsistent prioritization, missed SLA expectations, and scope creep when requests hit engineering. We need a lightweight, repeatable rubric with automation hooks in Linear/CRM to standardize initial scoring and routing.
goals: 1) Define a scoring rubric (security/regulatory weight, SLA urgency, customer ARR/strategic value, implementation complexity, runtime cost delta). 2) Add required fields to intake form. 3) Automate an initial score + labels in Linear. 4) Pilot with 5 enterprise customers and iterate. 5) Map score thresholds to priority buckets (P0/P1/P2) and deployment paths (hosted/dedicated/private).
acceptance_criteria: - A documented rubric stored in Confluence with scoring breakdown and examples. - Intake form updated in the CRM + onboarding docs; entries automatically create Linear tickets with pre-populated initial score and labels. - Automation rules in Linear that assign a tentative priority and route to the Hosted API triage queue. - Pilot completed with 5 enterprise customers and at least two real requests processed through the rubric end-to-end. - Engineering and Security review gates are defined for requests scoring above the security threshold. - Playbook for CS/Sales handoff and communication to customers is published.
notes: Initial stakeholder interviews: CS reported ~12 ambiguous asks last quarter; Sales prioritized 3 deals where feature SLAs materially impacted contract terms. Security flagged function-calling requests that may require HSM/KMS integration and audit logging. Running cost estimates indicate some streaming/low-latency tool-call requests could increase token and GPU footprint by 20-60% depending on batching changes.
tradeoffs: Strict gating reduces scope creep and sets clear customer expectations but could slow time-to-first-demo for sales. A lighter weight 'fast-track' for strategic accounts is included in the rubric to balance speed vs. risk. Automation accuracy will depend on quality of CRM metadata; initial pilot may require manual overrides.
decisions: - Adopt a 0-100 numeric score composed of five weighted dimensions: security/regulatory (30%), SLA/latency urgency (25%), customer value (20%), implementation effort (15%), runtime cost delta (10%). - Thresholds: >=85 => P0 + expedited engineering review; 65-84 => P1; 40-64 => P2 backlog; <40 => informational/backlog. - Requests with security score >=20 automatically require Security review before engineering estimates. - Route requests scoring >=70 and with enterprise ARR > $100k to a dedicated intake sub-route for Hosted vs Dedicated deployment decision.
risks: Scoring may be gamed by stakeholders if incentives misaligned. Automation depends on consistent CRM tagging; poor data will surface false positives/negatives. Security review capacity needs to scale with pilot volume. Initial thresholds are heuristic and will require calibration during the pilot.
next_steps: 1) Draft rubric doc and 6 canonical examples (Aisha) - due 2026-03-17 (PM-41280). 2) Update CRM intake form and Linear automation spec (Markus + Eng infra) - due 2026-03-24 (ENG-50211). 3) Schedule pilot with 5 customers identified by CS (CS lead: Elena Moroz) - start 2026-03-25. 4) Security review capacity plan (Security: Priya Rao) - due 2026-03-22. 5) Build dashboard to track incoming scores and routing (Analytics: Wei Zhou) - due 2026-03-30.
